open_questions: Interior variant polarity is read from behaviour, not from a streaming block (none was extracted): bugfixing, q305 and the gated vendor state all set interior=1 for the shop/den, so 1 is taken as the occupied look. Confirm on tour that interior=1 shows an open shop and not a quest-only overlay.

The four ExplosiveTriggerDeviceControllerPS mines are only made safe by a gated ForceSafeForPlayer node. Door states are unresolved in the catalogue (no cooked props, positions null). The storefront glass door and the sliding door should be usable through the runtime policy; the journal door should be the vanilla Body-check door, not the q305 seal. Tour-check all three.

Chang's jpn_05_A chair pose is a netrunner-chair netrun animation, i.e. working, not the gig's unresponsive slump. Confirm he does not spawn with the gig's aphasia/disabled state or a 'wake up' scene without the quest.

communities.why: The whole two-person sidewalk pair (LowlifeWoman x2) leaning on the wall by the shop, in their only phase A, activated exactly as vanilla does. They are ordinary passers-by on the block, and their spots sit inside the street-story section this proposal already loads, so they cost nothing.

variant_toggles.why: Raises the shop's gameplay interior so the basement den rooms (Chang's work area, the corridor and the devices) exist as a normal open shop instead of the closed/burned default. Vanilla never sets this in the open world: the gig's bugfix phase sets interior=1 to keep the interior present after the story, the Phantom Liberty Chang meeting sets it so his shop looks open, and the kept vendor phase sets it for his netrunner-vendor state. 1 is therefore the occupied-shop value.

The den's normal, calm lighting: the open-world and street-story phases switch the safe lighting on and the q305 meeting explicitly clears the danger lighting; the danger variant is only raised in the gig's alerted branch (gated). With no gig, the den should be lit for work, not red-alert.

proximity_wait.why: The computer in Chang's den (ComputerControllerPS, ForceON, full path under #loc_sts_wbr_jpn_05_gameplay/#loc_sts_wbr_jpn_05_devices) is the device vanilla drives right where the netrunner works and the only occupant stands, so it streams in with the den interior the toggles raise. A device, not a workspot (rule 8).
